public_health_question.v: How was the phased transition from Epi Info to DHIS2 for vaccine-preventable disease surveillance implemented across WHO African Region countries during 2019–2023?

ev.q: This report describes the phased transition from Epi Info to DHIS2 IDSR and case-based surveillance packages in WHO African Region countries during 2019–2023
Vaccine-preventable disease (VPD) surveillance is critical to public health because it provides data for timely detection of and response to VPD cases and outbreaks

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension (race, SES, rurality, sex, age, disability or other) appears; the report concerns country-level surveillance software, and the WHO African Region setting is a characteristic, not an equity reading.

notes: An implementation-status report with no tables and no health-outcome quantities; the counts are countries adopting software packages, so data_focus is none. Method fields are left empty per the brief, and condition_group reflects the VPD surveillance subject rather than an analysed exposure or outcome.
view_issues: The abbreviations list includes CAR, CBS, DRC and VPDS, which do not appear in the text; 'wthout' is a typo in the Discussion. Country-status figures are unverified self-reports, as the Limitations state.
